import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Load the dataset from the provided string
data = """amount,is_fraud,transaction_type,hour_of_day
115.02,0,refund,22
44.37,0,payment,5
144.25,0,transfer,21
536.22,0,payment,17
38.43,0,payment,5"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Since the provided sample data only contains non-fraudulent transactions (is_fraud=0),
# we will visualize the distributions of the other features.
# A multi-panel plot will show the overall characteristics of the observed transactions.

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(18, 5))
fig.suptitle('Distribution of Transaction Features (All Non-Fraudulent in Sample)', fontsize=16)

# Plot 1: Distribution of 'amount'
sns.histplot(df['amount'], kde=True, ax=axes[0], bins=len(df['amount'].unique()))
axes[0].set_title('Distribution of Transaction Amount')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Amount')
axes[0].set_ylabel('Frequency')

# Plot 2: Distribution of 'transaction_type'
sns.countplot(x='transaction_type', data=df, ax=axes[1], palette='viridis', order=df['transaction_type'].value_counts().index)
axes[1].set_title('Distribution of Transaction Type')
axes[1].set_xlabel('Transaction Type')
axes[1].set_ylabel('Count')

# Plot 3: Distribution of 'hour_of_day'
# Ensure all hours are represented for a complete picture, even if some have zero counts.
# However, with very small data, just showing observed hours is more practical.
sns.countplot(x='hour_of_day', data=df, ax=axes[2], palette='magma', order=sorted(df['hour_of_day'].unique()))
axes[2].set_title('Distribution of Hour of Day')
axes[2].set_xlabel('Hour of Day')
axes[2].set_ylabel('Count')

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95]) # Adjust layout to prevent title overlap
plt.savefig('output.png')
plt.close(fig) # Close the plot to free memory
